datasources.title: Data sources
datasources.lead: Connections to the databases and services that Kalzit queries.
datasources.empty.title: No data sources yet
datasources.empty.text: Add a data source to query it in Explore and in dashboards. PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB, SQL Server, SQLite and Prometheus are available.
datasources.empty.textReadOnly: Here are the data sources your role or access given to you lets you use. An admin adds them and gives access.
datasources.noOrg.title: No organization
datasources.noOrg.text: Data sources belong to an organization. Ask an admin to add you to one.
datasources.forbidden.title: No access
datasources.forbidden.text: Your role cannot see data sources. Dashboards shared with you still show their data.
datasources.forbidden.textWrite: Only admins add and change data sources.
datasources.deleted: The data source moved to the trash. Dashboards that use it show an error until you restore it.
datasources.column.name: Name
datasources.new.title: Add data source
datasources.new.lead: Choose the kind of database or service, then enter how Kalzit reaches it.
datasources.edit.title: Data source
datasources.readOnly.lead: Use a database login that can only read. Kalzit rejects queries that change data, but a read-only login is the real protection.
datasources.form.name: Name
datasources.form.nameRequired: Enter a name for the data source.
datasources.form.number: Enter a whole number of 0 or more.
datasources.form.unknownKind: This kind of data source is not available on this server.
datasources.secret.hint: Stored encrypted and never shown again.
datasources.secret.replaceHint: Replaces the stored value when you save. It is stored encrypted and never shown again.
datasources.delete.title: Delete data source?
datasources.delete.text: “{name}” moves to the trash. Panels that query it show an error until it is restored.
datasources.editor.label: Query
datasources.editor.shortcuts: Ctrl+Enter runs the query, Ctrl+Space shows suggestions.
datasources.editor.schemaFailed: The schema could not be loaded, so suggestions cover keywords only.
datasources.editor.unsupported: There is no query editor for this kind of data source yet.
datasources.editor.macrosLead: Macros take the dashboard time range. Kalzit passes them as parameters, never as text in the query.
datasources.editor.macro.timeFilter: True for rows whose column lies in the time range.
datasources.editor.macro.interval: Suggested grouping interval for the time range, such as 1m.
datasources.editor.instant: Instant query: one value per series at the end of the time range
datasources.editor.kind.label: label
datasources.form.nameTaken: Another data source already has this name. Choose a different one.
datasources.trash.title: Data source trash
datasources.trash.lead: Deleted data sources stay here. Restore one to use it again in Explore and dashboards.
datasources.editor.sqlHint: One SELECT or WITH statement. Variables are written $name and reach the database as parameters.
datasources.editor.promHint: Variables only inside quoted strings, such as job=“$job”.
datasources.editor.minStepInvalid: Enter a number of seconds, such as 15.
datasources.editor.promMacrosLead: Macros take the time range of the dashboard or of Explore.
datasources.editor.macro.rateInterval: Four intervals, at least 1m: a safe window for rate().
datasources.editor.macro.range: The length of the time range.
datasources.editor.macro.timeFromSeconds: Start of the time range in Unix seconds.
datasources.editor.macro.timeToSeconds: End of the time range in Unix seconds.
datasources.settings.trustServerCertific: Trust the server certificate without checking it (only for tests)
datasources.settings.hosts: Hosts (host or host:port, separated by commas)
datasources.settings.srv: Look up the servers in DNS (mongodb+srv)
datasources.kinds.postgres.hint: Use a login that can only read, for example a role with only SELECT rights such as a member of pg_read_all_data. Kalzit rejects queries that change data, but a read-only login is the real protection.
datasources.kinds.mysql.hint: Use a user with only the SELECT privilege on the databases you need. Kalzit rejects queries that change data, but a read-only login is the real protection.
datasources.kinds.mssql.hint: Use a login in the db_datareader role only. Kalzit rejects queries that change data, but a read-only login is the real protection.
datasources.kinds.sqlite.hint: Kalzit opens SQLite files read-only, and only from folders a server admin allowed.
datasources.kinds.prometheus.hint: Use credentials that can only read, if your server needs any.
datasources.kinds.mongodb.hint: Use a login with only the read role on this database. Kalzit refuses logins that may do more, and servers without access control.
datasources.secret.reenter: The connection target changed, so enter this again (or remove it) before saving. Kalzit never sends a stored secret to a new target unasked.
datasources.form.readOnlyAccess: You may use this data source but not change it. An admin can give you edit access.
datasources.form.targetLocked: You may change the name, limits and secrets. Where the source connects (host, port, user, TLS, URL or path) only a data source admin can change.

datasources.reason.variables.too_many: A dashboard has at most {max} variables.

datasources.kinds.file.hint: Kalzit only reads the file, and only from folders a server admin allowed for files.
datasources.kinds.http_json.hint: Kalzit sends only GET requests. Use a token that can only read.
